verdict_by_component.scoping_protocol: PASS_WITH_LIMITATIONS (may be executed; negative overall result must be read as not determinable)

review_limits: SPEC-1bb, HYPOTHESES, IDENTIFIABILITY, CONFORMANCE-CASE and STATE are not permitted inputs, so UNCHANGED marks, CHANGELOG 'before' entries and source quotes cannot be checked against the originals.
Statements about git behaviour come from knowledge of git, not from running it; confidence is stated per issue.

defects_notes.D1: Six distinctions, NIF tiers, G-D1 and the per-prediction matrix are real. But NIF-B is behavioural and both hypotheses explain it (N1); G-D1 misses the act-exclusivity premise (N2); the fallback is applied asymmetrically (N3).
defects_notes.D2: The two-stage design and O0 are real. The outcome table is neither exhaustive nor exclusive, and O5 lacks the not-ACC condition (N7). O0 wrongly drops P4 (N8).
defects_notes.D4: Fixed. Residual: waivers recorded before the window start are not acquired (N10).
defects_notes.D5: (b) late recording is not operational, because S1-b is bounded by the window and acts that do not state an effect date are not covered (N9). (c) The 'already governs' classification is frozen against H-D without a scored sensitivity result (N4).
defects_notes.D6: Fixed. The promised check of R-91/R-94 referring to R11 is not a Stage 1 item (N11).
defects_notes.D8: Named fields added. The P1 satisfaction rule is deferred, not frozen (N12). The rest of the review JSON cannot be checked because it is not an input.
defects_notes.D9: The fallback is only a lower bound and conflicts with M-TIME, and the verdicts are not exclusive (N5). An absence that is not shown gives NON-CONFORMS (N6). The default carries H-D (N2).
defects_notes.D13: Fixed as the reviewer asked, but FR-D13(2) relies on NIF-B, so N1 carries over.

new_defects.defect: Third-party application (NIF-B) is behaviour that both hypotheses explain (H-D: the third party acted contrary to the norm or erred; H-B: practice changed the norm). Yet it establishes N-FORCE[OPERATIONAL] and fires P4-HD in O3. This collapses distinction 4 into distinction 2. Downgrading only when the application is expressly voided makes silence count as force.
new_defects.fix: Extend G-D1 to any behaviour. A force premise that rests only on NIF-B is DISJUNCTIVE. Only NIF-A can give FIRED.

new_defects.where: §0.3 ACT-CONTRA; graded fallback; FR-D9 default; O5 baseline
new_defects.defect: G-D1 catches only H-D's status rule. The inference 'no permitting act in a complete DCS => not permitted' presupposes H-D's act-exclusivity clause (P1). Under H-B reading 1, a permission can arise from work without an act. So P2, C1 and O5 falsify H-B on an H-D premise.
new_defects.fix: Add G-D1(c): a non-permission premise derived from the absence of a permitting act grades DISJUNCTIVE {H-D P1, H-B conformance} unless NIF-A shows the state.

new_defects.where: §1.7 P2, P5-HB and P7 rows vs the P4 row
new_defects.defect: The maker's records are admitted as a FIRED-CONDITIONAL fallback against H-B, but a maker force assertion is barred even conditionally against H-D. TASK requires NIF or NON-DISCRIMINATING; the fallback is neither, and it is offered to one side only.
new_defects.fix: Apply the fallback symmetrically or not at all.

new_defects.defect: The sole adopter's 'R-89 already governs' is frozen as non-adoption, and the sensitivity result is never scored. Together with N1, O3 falsifies H-D in a scenario H-D explains (the DA declares R-89 governing and a third party applies it).
new_defects.fix: Label the classification PROPOSAL/UNKNOWN. Score O3 only if it holds under both classifications; otherwise FIRED-CONDITIONAL.

new_defects.defect: 'Not earlier than recording time' is not implied by the inputs (decision and effect can precede recording) and is only a lower bound. So 'in force before 16:10' can never be shown. P is then unshowable, and NON-CONFORMS and UNDETERMINED can hold at once, so the verdict is not a function.
new_defects.fix: Give the verdicts a precedence with UNDETERMINED first. Without an upper bound on entry into force, P and B are NOT_IDENTIFIABLE.

new_defects.defect: Showing P requires an absence that §0.8 makes practically unshowable. Failing to show it gives NON-CONFORMS, so an H-B falsifier fires on NOT-EVIDENCED-IN-CAPTURE. This contradicts §0.8, FR-D5(e) and D9's own sufficiency claim.
new_defects.fix: An absence that is not evidenced gives UNDETERMINED.

new_defects.defect: No row for {trace cites R-89, ACC, not AD, no NIF} or for not-G. MENTION_ONLY and CAPTURE_ERROR are unmapped. O5 lacks not-ACC, so it fires P7-HB/P2 when WP-4B acceptance is in force and the gate is satisfied. The joint firing of O2 and O3, and the precedence of O6, are unstated.
new_defects.fix: Rebuild the table as an ordered decision procedure; add not-ACC to O5.

new_defects.defect: After D1, P4-HD (O3) no longer depends on work, but O0 drops P4 and S1-e/S1-f run only if a WP-4C-1 trace exists.
Acts recorded after the window are never acquired, so the late-recording rule cannot fire. Late-recorded acts that do not state an effect date are not covered.
new_defects.fix: Read the full DCS history up to capture; treat post-window acts on the target as possibly late.

new_defects.defect: Waivers recorded before the window start are not acquired, although 'no waiver in force at t_w-' needs them.
new_defects.fix: Read the waiver history from the root.

new_defects.defect: The check of R-91/R-94 referring to R11 is promised but appears in no Stage 1 item, and Stage 1 is gated on a WP-4C-1 trace.
new_defects.fix: Add it as a P8 item, not gated.

new_defects.defect: The per-clause satisfaction rule is deferred to 'before Stage 1', so it is not frozen now. The eligibility definition also derives H-B's work condition from the text of acts.
new_defects.fix: Freeze the rules now, or mark P1 NOT_FROZEN.

new_defects.defect: The grade vocabulary omits NON-DISCRIMINATING, LEGITIMATED, VACUOUS, ONE-SIDED and NOT_TESTABLE_AS_SPECIFIED. N-KNOWN is 'known or claimed', which merges factive knowledge with assertion. DCS v1 membership is inconsistent (NORM_STATE).

instances: NIF-B (third-party application) fires P4-HD in O3 and establishes N-FORCE elsewhere (N1).
The absence of a permitting act is used to establish non-permission against H-B (ACT-CONTRA, fallback, C1 default, O5) without G-D1 protection (N2).
d1_assessment.fallback_note: The graded fallback (the maker's records) is not an independent observable. It is offered for the H-B limbs only (N3), which departs from TASK's 'NIF or NON-DISCRIMINATING'.

six_distinctions.norm_in_force: partly collapsed: established by NIF-B (distinction 4 -> 2) and by absence of a text (distinction 1 -> 2 via ACT-CONTRA)
six_distinctions.act_according_to: kept for the executor; merged into in-force for third parties
six_distinctions.act_contrary_to: partly: derivable from 'no permitting act', which presupposes H-D P1
six_distinctions.change_without_act: mostly kept; with NIF-B, it reduces to a change in third-party behaviour

smuggling.HD: PARTIAL: through the act-exclusivity baseline ('no permitting act => not permitted') in ACT-CONTRA, the graded fallback, the FR-D9 default and O5 (N2), and through the asymmetric admission of the maker's records against H-B only (N3).
smuggling.HB: YES (overcorrection in P4/O3): NIF-B treats practice as force (N1), and the sole adopter's 'already governs' is frozen as non-adoption with an unscored sensitivity result (N4). Together they let P4-HD fire in an H-D-consistent scenario.

rank0_protocol.target_matching: Over-inclusive via ET-1/ET-2 mentions and governance data files (R0-5). Under-inclusive via untokened work (disclosed), ref names (R0-8), multibyte hyphens (R0-4) and unfetched MR/PR refs (R0-2). The exclusions are correct.
rank0_protocol.trace_vs_mention_operational: In principle yes (path-class rule plus message position), but miscalibrated (R0-5) and not operational for merges (R0-6).

issues.issue: Run B runs rank0-wp4c1.sh in a bare mirror clone. 'git rev-parse --show-toplevel' dies outside a work tree (git >= 2.25; the prerequisite is >= 2.31), and set -e aborts the script at 00_env.txt.
issues.failure_scenario: Every Run B gives CAPTURE_ERROR under W5. PRIMARY results come from Run B, so no valid output is possible; the reviewer's R2 rerun fails the same way. Ad-hoc fixes are forbidden.

issues.confidence: high (GitHub refs/pull/*/merge); high (GitLab refs/merge-requests of squash-merged or deleted branches)
issues.issue: The C2 check lists all advertised refs with ls-remote, but the fetch uses the default refspecs only.
issues.failure_scenario: A hosted repository with PRs or MRs gives MISSING in 08_remote_objects.txt, so C2 fails and the capture is CAPTURE_INVALID. Unmerged or squashed MR work on WP-4C-1 is never searched, although B.1 claims all refs. refs/notes is claimed but not fetched.

issues.issue: 15_paths.txt hits are not in 90_hitset.txt, so the ET-2 path clause has no details or ancestry. Such ETs would appear ancestry-minimal in rank0-order.sh when they are not.
Under LC_ALL=C, VAR's [^0-9a-z]{0,2} counts bytes. U+2010, U+2011 and U+2013 are 3 bytes, so non-ASCII-hyphen variants are missed, contrary to B.2.

Over-inclusion: ET-1 fires on a subject mention in another WP's commit (MIXED has no effect on the class), and on governance data files (register.yaml, queue.json) that fall outside DOC_GOV. ET-2 fires on TODO comments. A plan or ruling can become t_w, the premise of P7-HB.
Merge ET-1 rule 'NON_DOC changes not present in any other hit commit' has no identity criterion.

No script computes CLOCK_ANOMALY. Global git config is not isolated (GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL). The byte-identity claim is false because 00_env and 04_remotes hold machine-specific paths. W7 classification is manual; this is acceptable only because R3 codes blind.
Ref names such as feature/WP-4C-1 are not matched against PAT.
Race between fetch and ls-remote. The awk path extraction truncates paths with spaces and maps deleted-file lines to /dev/null.

scoping_protocol.existence_only: essentially yes (CODEOWNERS contents are explicitly allowed); 58_path_history_meta outputs names and emails, contrary to C.1

issues.issue: NIF_A_CHANNEL_EXISTS is unreachable. Q5 = YES needs NORM_STATE, but Q2 is derived from channel type and K-STATUS is UNKNOWN_CONTENT. I2 needs content, so INDEPENDENT is unreachable. The result is fixed before the run.
Q5 has no UNKNOWN, so unread content is forced to NO. 'NO_NIF_A_CHANNEL_IN_CHECKED_SET' reads as a negative finding. Report it as NIF_A_NOT_DETERMINABLE_BY_EXISTENCE_CHECK.
Only paths in the current default-branch tree are checked. Files that existed during the window and were later deleted are missed; the 'ever-existed' comment is inaccurate.

K3 and Part B C3 need audit-log content that the script does not fetch. COMPLETE_SHOWN, ABSENT_IN_COMPLETE_CHANNEL and any complete DCS are therefore unreachable, so absence-premised falsifiers will be UNDETERMINED.
Author names and emails in 58_path_history_meta.txt contradict 'roles, not personal names'.
The completeness window is hard-coded to 2026-08-02..15, inconsistent with FR-D4 (no lower bound; the P7 window may start before R-72).
Host detection by URL substring misses self-hosted GitLab/GHE (disclosed as UNKNOWN). STATUS_RE is over-broad ('norm' matches 'normalize').

disagreements.point: 'No single observation can be counted for both sides' is false: NIF-B (N1) and the absence of a permitting act (N2) each serve both sides.
The outcome table is not exhaustive (N7).
'The default is never applied to evidence that has not been seen' is false (N6).
I agree with SPEC-r1 that citation shows only N-KNOWN. But application by a non-executor is equally dual-explainable; only NIF-A separates the limbs.

'NON-CONFORMS by default / unauthorized unless shown' presupposes H-D act-exclusivity and turns an absence that is not shown into a falsification (N2, N6). UNDETERMINED or DISJUNCTIVE is the defensible default.
The byte-identity and reproducibility claims are unsupported (R0-7). Reproducibility rests only on the canonical key, and only once R0-1 is fixed.

P4+P7 HIGH is optimistic. Given SC-1 and SC-4, NIF-A and complete-channel absences are unobtainable with the frozen tools, so the realistic outcomes are NON-DISCRIMINATING, DISJUNCTIVE or UNDETERMINED.

rank0_r2: run Run B in a non-bare clone of the bundle, or guard --show-toplevel
fetch +refs/*:refs/*, or restrict C2 to the fetched refspec and declare MR/PR refs in or out of channel
add path-pass hits to the hit set
recalibrate ET-1/ET-2 (MIXED, governance data files, comments)
compute CLOCK_ANOMALY; set GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null; match PAT against ref names
spec: N3: apply the fallback symmetrically or not at all
N4: score O3 under both AF readings
N5/N6: verdict precedence; an absence that is not shown gives UNDETERMINED
N7/N8: rebuild the outcome table; ungate P4
N9-N12: full-history S1-b, R-91/R-94 item, freeze the P1 rules
scoping: add UNKNOWN to Q5; rename the negative overall result
optional r2: historical paths; drop names and emails from 58
